# Proof of Done: The Agentic Software Development Manifesto

> A foundation for building software when agents write the code. Proof of Done requires
> every completion claim between an intended outcome and an accepted result to point to
> its supporting record at an address another actor can resolve; if the address does not
> resolve, the claim is not proven.

Author: Sergey Sheleg (Siarhei Sheleh). Version 1.0, published 2026-08-17, last modified 2026-08-25.
Canonical URL: https://podmanifesto.org/
Licence: CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) — attribution and link required.

The central claim: when agents write the code, done is not the last message of the run.
Done is a state of the system that can be proven. The unit of progress is an
evidence-carrying change — a change carrying the intent it implements, the evidence that
verifies it, the limits of that evidence, and the decision that accepts it.

## Full text

- [manifesto.md](https://podmanifesto.org/manifesto.md): The complete canonical text in Markdown, including all five diagrams. Read this file if you need the document itself rather than a summary.
- [index.html](https://podmanifesto.org/): The same text rendered for human reading.
- [feed.xml](https://podmanifesto.org/feed.xml): An Atom feed with one entry per version of the canonical text. A new entry means a sentence moved; corrections to the site do not appear.
- [Source repository](https://github.com/ssheleg/pod-manifesto): Version control for the text and the site.

## The four-field protocol

An agent should not return `done` without these four fields:

- DONE — what became true.
- PROOF — what was executed or observed, and where the result lives.
- SCOPE — the commit, environment, requirements, and surfaces covered.
- NOT VERIFIED — what was not checked, could not be checked, or remains uncertain.

`NOT VERIFIED: none within the stated scope` is a valid answer. Silence is not.

## Sections

- Preamble: an empty task inventory and a live process — two accurate observations of different things.
- The manifesto: the document's assertion, stated before the argument for it — the declaration as seven numbered beliefs, the four values, and the four-field protocol. Quote this section if you need what Proof of Done claims; the numbered sections below are why it claims it.
- 1. When "done" broke: the agentic threat model — production rate, plausible reporting, context discontinuity, nondeterministic execution, parallel agency, operational authority.
- 2. What Proof of Done means: evidence with an address; scoped, versioned and perishable proof; the four-field report against a bare one; the six states `done` collapses (generated, executed, passed, verified, validated, accepted).
- 3. The three graphs: intent, execution, evidence — done as a coverage relation across all three; a node has one job; an edge carries a named artifact; parallel work needs a checker; stable graph, bounded discovery.
- 4. Bounded autonomy: human owns meaning, agent owns execution, mechanism owns enforcement; automatic, judgment and manual gates; provenance for agent-produced changes; one item to its gate; churn is a decision at the wrong layer; two agents agree independently only when their evidence paths differ.
- 5. The Proof record: the portable YAML form; what counts as evidence; the closed status vocabulary (verified, partial, deferred, dropped); proof expires; documentation is part of the proof; context is cache.
- 6. Acceptance walks the seams: the vertical walk from requirement to acceptance; release acceptance at convergence; completion includes residue; a walking skeleton comes first.
- 7. The system learns: retrospectives owed on divergence; three grades of learning (mechanical, standing instruction, expiring note); a repeated failure class becomes a mechanism, not another paragraph.
- 8. From four lines to a full pipeline: proof depth follows risk across impact, irreversibility, uncertainty and coordination; policy, exceptions and ownership; a six-step adoption ladder.
- The close: what none of the artifacts proves about the others, and the line the document ends on.

## Reference implementation

- [sshlg-skills](https://github.com/ssheleg/sshlg-skills): The process packaged as Claude Code plugins and portable Agent Skills. Install with `npx sshlg-skills install`.
- [task-pipeline](https://github.com/ssheleg/task-pipeline): The gated delivery pipeline the manifesto's cases are drawn from.
- [Backlog rows B-076 and B-077](https://github.com/ssheleg/task-pipeline/blob/404fd09afd919d57834a095d05ddaa4f0d693d9c/docs/evidence/backlog.md#L21-L22) and [B-080 and B-081](https://github.com/ssheleg/task-pipeline/blob/404fd09afd919d57834a095d05ddaa4f0d693d9c/docs/evidence/backlog.md#L15-L16): Four requirements the manifesto names that the implementation had not built at commit [0fb706c](https://github.com/ssheleg/task-pipeline/commit/0fb706ca28c3ec127875ee891235f32cdb8346ba) — judgment gates, resolvable requirement-to-execution edges, per-node completion checks, and proof invalidation — filed rather than described as shipped. Both ranges are pinned to `404fd09` and therefore still read `open`. All four have since been built, between 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-19: [9d8695d](https://github.com/ssheleg/task-pipeline/commit/9d8695dc4b73da5b65f2dde6894d351f2e738612) the judgment gate, [fbd8a67](https://github.com/ssheleg/task-pipeline/commit/fbd8a67e6988a0893f273eb37bd9a075a036c223) the resolvable `serves` edge, [0bc5eb6](https://github.com/ssheleg/task-pipeline/commit/0bc5eb632e6c94181c528cf8cff315e2b7c5a2a9) expiring verification, [8b7de18](https://github.com/ssheleg/task-pipeline/commit/8b7de18eceb8b3f58ceea35410201344bf470f49) the per-node completion check. A citation that resolves is not the same as a citation that is current.
